message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic, modern, and cult‑favorite horror films you might enjoy:

| Year | Title | Why it’s worth watching |
|------|-------|------------------------|
| 1960 | **Psycho** (dir. Alfred Hitchcock) | A masterclass in suspense and psychological terror. |
| 1968 | **Night of the Living Dead** (dir. George A. Romero) | The original zombie film that defined a genre. |
| 1974 | **The Exorcist** (dir. William Friedkin) | One of the most chilling supernatural thrillers ever made. |
| 1980 | **The Shining** (dir. Stanley Kubrick) | A haunting psychological horror with iconic imagery. |
| 1984 | **A Nightmare on Elm Street** (dir. Wes Craven) | Introduced the terrifying Freddy Krueger. |
| 1991 | **The Silence of the Lambs** (dir. Jonathan Demme) | A tense thriller blending crime and horror. |
| 1999 | **The Blair Witch Project** (dir. Daniel Myrick & Eduardo Sánchez) | Pioneered the found‑footage style. |
| 2002 | **28 Days Later** (dir. Danny Boyle) | A fast‑paced, post‑apocalyptic zombie film. |
| 2004 | **Saw** (dir. James Wan) | A gritty, puzzle‑based horror that sparked a franchise. |
| 2007 | **Paranormal Activity** (dir. Oren Peli) | Low‑budget found‑footage that made a huge impact. |
| 2010 | **The Conjuring** (dir. James Wan) | A modern supernatural horror with strong storytelling. |
| 2012 | **The Cabin in the Woods** (dir. Drew Goddard) | A meta‑take on horror tropes that’s both funny and scary. |
| 2014 | **It Follows** (dir. David Robert Mitchell) | A fresh take on the “invisible threat” concept. |
| 2015 | **The Witch** (dir. Robert Eggers) | A slow‑burning, atmospheric period horror. |
| 2017 | **Get Out** (dir. Jordan Peele) | A socially conscious horror with sharp satire. |
| 2018 | **A Quiet Place** (dir. John Krasinski) | Tension built around silence and sound. |
| 2019 | **Midsommar** (dir. Ari Aster) | A daylight horror that’s unsettling in a different way. |
| 2020 | **The Invisible Man** (dir. Leigh Whannell) | A modern retelling with strong feminist themes. |
| 2021 | **Candyman** (dir. Nia DaCosta) | A fresh take on a classic urban legend. |
| 2022 | **The Black Phone** (dir. Scott Derrickson) | A supernatural thriller with a unique premise. |
| 2023 | **M3GAN** (dir. Gerard Johnstone) | A horror‑comedy about a creepy AI doll. |

Feel free to pick based on your preferred sub‑genre—psychological, supernatural, slasher, or something more experimental. Enjoy the chills!
